pr_title: Fix regression around commas in commit titles during `pr create`
pr_body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8719

In `v2.44.0` the `--fill-verbose` flag was introduced in order to include title and body information in a PR. Unfortunately, the string handling logic to break apart the output from `git log` was incorrect. It was relying on a format of `sha,title,body` and assuming that the title did not contain any commas. This was a mistake, and resulted in trailing text being discarded.

This PR asks `git log` to use the null byte as a separator, which we don't think is an allowable character in a git commit:

```
➜ git commit
error: a NUL byte in commit log message not allowed.
fatal: failed to write commit object
```

It additionally updates the commit parsing logic to better handle newlines in the commit body, where the previous version had a bug for bodies of the form:

```
Title

Body
<git sha> some more text
```

Where the `<git sha>` following a newline would be interpreted as an entirely new commit. This bug was never surfaced, I just confirmed it when reading the code.

issue_context.title: Problem parsing comma when using: `gh pr create --fill`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When I ran `gh pr create --fill` I had one commit on the branch with a msg like this:

```
Testing one, two, three

More details and some paragraphs here.
```

It looks like the CLI created the PR title with everything up to the first comma:

`Testing one`

Then the body/description for the PR included the rest of the first line in the body:

```
two, threeMore details and some paragraphs here.
```

So it was split after the first comma.

gh version 2.44.1 (2024-02-16)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.44.1

This might relate somewhat to this issue although I'm not sure:
https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8706

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Create a branch with a single commit that has comma in the first line of the commit message. Then:
```
gh pr create --fill
```


### Expected vs actual behavior

I would expect the whole first line of the commit message to be used as the subject for the PR. Not just the text up until the first comma.
comments:
Thanks for opening this issue and apologies for breaking you.

I believe I can see why this would happen with the change from #8423 which I think makes some bad assumptions about commas: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/8423/files#diff-ccedca01e076cd065987253b366873ca2bee2e28c9d0bc13d50d7b7795c0bf4eR252

This is the second bug this PR has caused so I'm leaning towards reverting it.
#8768 was merged yesterday, so a fix should go out in our next release. I would anticipate that being Tuesday.

review_comments:
**Why is the additional null byte separate after the body necessary?**

I only ask because we're not checking the size of the split line nor using that index in the code below.

It might not be necessary anymore!

I added it because when the regex said `[\S\s]*` it would greedily consume the rest of the string including the newlines.

However, now that I've made it lazy with `?` I think it might stop at `$`

I'll check!

Oh no, this doesn't work because for [commit bodies with newlines](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/8768/files#diff-e0d3414f3f705f5bcd834cfa70ffcab2ac76b2a44b4f1a67331bacf5599722e9R579-R607), the regex without the final `%x00` will either lazily stop at `$` (i.e. the newline in the commit body):

```
var commitLogRE = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}\x00.*?\x00[\S\s]*?$`)
```

```
[]string len: 2, cap: 10, ["6a6872b918c601a0e730710ad8473938a7516d30\x00testing testability test\x00This is the body","7a6872b918c601a0e730710ad8473938a7516d31\x00testing testability test 2\x00This is the body 2"]
```

See that it's missing the `\nwith a newline` from the first entry.

Or it will greedily consume to the end of all the commit logs:

```
var commitLogRE = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}\x00.*?\x00[\S\s]*$`)
```

```
[]string len: 1, cap: 10, ["6a6872b918c601a0e730710ad8473938a7516d30\x00testing testability test\x00This is the body\nwith a newline\n7a6872b918c601a0e730710ad8473938a7516d31\x00testing testability test 2\x00This is the body 2\n"]
```
